_README: NINE DRAFTED ROWS — the second tranche, chaining one and two pages beyond
the rows the 2026-09-04 widening verified (works.json, 11 rows since
84a5ccac). Drafted 2026-09-05 on branch claude/scan-gate-rows-2; every row
needs Sean's confirmation against the print before it can score. The human
step is minutes per row — see ROW_VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST_2026-09-05.md, and
every printed number a check cites has a zoomed crop in crops-2026-09-05/
(that directory name avoids the repo-wide `benchmarks/**/crops/` gitignore
rule, which exists for heavy regenerable labeling crops; these are small
committed evidence images).
KEPT OUT OF works.json ON PURPOSE, same mechanics as works-drafts.json:
scan_eval.py runs every works.json row whose window is complete and then
WITHHOLDS the pooled figure while any scored row's confidence is not
'verified'. A draft merged into works.json would be transcribed on the next
default run AND take the pooled gate number away from every session.
scan_eval.py reads only works.json (WORKS = BENCH / 'works.json'), so this
file cannot leak into the pool by construction. The widened 10-row gate
baselines (WIDENED_BASELINE_2026-09-04.md: prior-prod 0.8457/29081,
production 0.8387/29082) are untouched.
TO PROMOTE A ROW: confirm its `check` list against the print, move the row
into works.json's `rows`, set window.confidence to 'verified', and record
what was confirmed in window.verified_by (VERIFICATION.md gets the story).
No row here replaces an existing works.json row — all nine are new pages.
WHY THESE ARE CHEAP: every page chains from a window verified on 09-04, and
seven of the nine carry the engraver's own system-start measure numbers
(Litolff 984073: 49/65 then 83/98 then 113; Breitkopf Brahms: 23/29 then
38/48 then 59/70; Peters Mahler: 17, 24, 32 — each printed TWICE per page).
The two that don't: the 575951 Beethoven reprint (numbers transfer from the
twin by plate identity, re-fingerprinted per page below) and the Simrock
Dvorak (no numbers on the plate — the one counting row, with numbered
counting strips cut from the transcription's own cell boundaries).
Evidence classes used per row (each row's window.verified_by lists its own):
- printed system-start measure numbers, read off the scan at 400-450 dpi
by the drafting session (crops committed for every one Sean must read);
- the pipeline's own per-staff measure counts (unanimity reported, never
trusted alone — the 0.8706-against-17 lesson; two rows below show WHY:
mahler-p4 reads 8 unanimous where the engraver printed 7, and
575951-p4 reads 16 unanimous in system 1 where the print says 15);
- reference activity grids (verify_window.py), checked in BOTH directions;
- reference trims (trim_reference.py) proving the window exists in the
truth file with the right measure numbers (repeat strips explained
where they occur);
- reference-side engraving facts with no shared failure mode with barline
counting: Brahms's intro-closing double bar at m37-right and the
m40-left exposition start-repeat; Dvorak's 2/4 + repeat-start +
'Allegro molto. M.M. 136' at m24;
- for the Beethoven twins, plate fingerprints per page: measure
boundaries normalised to system width, p.3 agreeing to 0.0014 with ZERO
unmatched boundaries on either side, p.4 localizing the high-res scan's
one split bar.
⚠️ draft_windows.py was run for the six chainable pages (both Brahms and
both 984073 Beethoven pages, the 575951 p.4 via its twin, Dvorak p.7); the
Mahler pages are hand-drafted (their base rows carry no `staves` list, the
same reason the promoted mahler-p3 row was hand-drafted). Its output needed
hand correction on ONE page, the same trap class as the 09-04 Brahms case:
on beethoven-984073-p4 both systems print 11 staves but NEITHER is the base
row's 11-staff lineup (system 1 suppresses Timpani and splits Vcl/Basso;
system 2 keeps Timpani and condenses the bottom staff), so the drafter's
positional pairing silently placed 'Timpani in C.G.' on the staff the print
labels as a violin — it flagged only the two staves where the margin read
disagreed. The corrected maps are in systems_as_printed with the trap noted
in `check`. On beethoven-984073-p3 the instrument pairing of the shorter
system 2 SUCCEEDED and was then corroborated against the reference rather
than trusted: the three staves it drops (Oboi, Trombe, Timpani) are exactly
the three parts the reference holds silent through mm 65-82.

rows.label: Beethoven 5 / Litolff-family / low-res bitonal — p.3, first tacet-suppressed Litolff page

verified_by: DRAFT 2026-09-05, not yet human-verified. Evidence assembled so far:

printed numbers 49 / 65 / 83 — three engraved facts agreeing with the chain (48+1=49) and with each other (65-49=16 bars in system 1, 83-65=18 in system 2, 34 measures on the page). Read at 450 dpi by the drafting session; crops b984073-p3-sys1-opens-49.png, b984073-p3-sys2-opens-65.png, b984073-p4-sys1-opens-83.png.
pipeline: 16 + 18 bars, unanimous across all 19 staves — agrees with the engraver exactly here (unlike p.2, where this raster drops one barline).

plate fingerprint against the twin 575951 p.3: all boundaries matched, ZERO unmatched on either side, max normalised disagreement 0.0013 (system 1, 17 boundaries) / 0.0014 (system 2, 19 boundaries) — the cleanest fingerprint of any page pair yet.
trim_reference: mm 49-82 = 34 measures numbered 49..82, no unmatched repeats, no invisible notes.

activity grid (verify_window over mm 49-82, context 2) matches the page in the discriminating directions: m57 is the ONLY all-parts-silent bar anywhere in mm 47-84 (the G.P. — page bar 9 of system 1), m58 sounds exactly ONE object in every part (the single ff chord — page bar 10), the Eb Horns then carry mm 59-62 ALONE (the second-theme horn call — bars 11-14); Violin 1's four-bar phrase mm 63-66 STRADDLES the system break (bars 15-16 of system 1 + bars 1-2 of system 2); Clarinet 1 answers mm 67-70, Flute 1 mm 71-74; Vc+Basso sound in two-bar pairs every four bars (65-66, 69-70, 73-74, 77-78, 81-82).

the three suppressed staves are exactly the parts the reference silences: Oboi last sound m58 and re-enter m84 (so their staff leaves at the system break and returns on p.4 — and it does), Trombe and Timpani last sound m56 and stay silent past the page (Trumpets/Timpani return only at m94/m98, both on p.4).

the closure in the other direction: m83 (NOT on this page) is the Clarinets' + Eb Horns' + full-string re-entry after the Vc/Cb pair at 81-82 — system 2's last bar must be the quiet pair, not the re-entry.
check: confirm the printed 49 above system 1 and 65 above system 2 (crops: b984073-p3-sys1-opens-49.png, b984073-p3-sys2-opens-65.png), and 83 opening p.4 (b984073-p4-sys1-opens-83.png)
confirm system 2 prints 8 staves, margins Fl. / Cl. / Fag. / Cor. then four unlabeled string staves — no Ob., no Tr., no Tp.

sanity glance, system 1: bar 9 is an empty G.P. bar, bar 10 a single ff chord in every part, bar 11 the horns alone (crop b984073-p3-mm56-59-gp-chord-horncall.png shows bars 8-11 of the top five staves)

printed numbers 83 / 98 / 113 agree with the chain (82+1=83) and with each other (98-83=15 bars in system 1, 113-98=15 in system 2, 30 measures on the page). the lineup changes are exactly what the reference plays: Timpani are silent mm 83-97 and their FIRST note after m56 is m98 — the bar system 2 opens on, which is why their staff exists only there; at m83 the reference has Violoncello sounding while Viola and Contrabass REST, and the print shows exactly that (rest / notes / rest in the first bar of the Viola / 'Vcl.' / 'Basso' staves — crop b984073-p4-margins-sys1-no-Tp-split-VclBasso.png; the engraver split Vcl from Basso at the page where their material diverges, then re-condensed as 'Bassi.' for system 2, crop b984073-p4-margins-sys2-with-Tp-Bassi.png).

rows.label: Mahler 5 / Edition Peters — p.4 (printed p.5), the funeral-march tutti

edition.publisher_as_catalogued: (unidentified scan 2016); the page itself says Edition Peters (plate 8951 at the foot)

page.n_staves_note: 18 FIVE-LINE staves plus 3 one-line percussion staves (Becken, Gr. Tr., Kl. Tr.) = 21 printed. Compare `detected` against 18. Margins: Hoboen 1.2.3, A-Klar. 1.2.3, Fag. 1/2, Contraf., F-Hörner 1.3.5, F-Hörner 2.4.6, B-Tromp. 1.2, B-Tromp. 3.4, Posaunen, Tuba, Pauken, [the three one-line rules], Erste Viol., Zweite Viol., Violen, Vcelle. get. (TWO staves), Bässe get. (TWO staves). Relative to p.3's 13: Hoboen and Pauken return (they sound from m17/m19), the celli and basses split divisi onto two staves each ('get.' = geteilt); no Tamtam rule yet (first sounds m27, on p.5).
